quizSynopsis: Test your knowledge of Docusaurus architecture, MDX integration, and React component workflows.

questions.question: Which technology allows you to write JSX inside standard Markdown files in Docusaurus?
questions.messageForCorrectAnswer: Correct! MDX blends Markdown and React seamlessly.
questions.messageForIncorrectAnswer: Incorrect. Docusaurus relies on MDX to render React elements.
questions.explanation: MDX lets you import and use UI components directly inside your documentation files.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used to add global interactive UI elements like banners or chatbots in Docusaurus?
questions.messageForCorrectAnswer: Spot on! You can write a custom plugin or inject functionality by swizzling existing themes.
questions.messageForIncorrectAnswer: Not quite. Remember that global features usually require deeper integration.
questions.explanation: Plugins let you hook into the client lifecycle, while Swizzling allows you to override default theme components.

questions.question: Select all valid built-in interactive components provided by native Docusaurus themes:
questions.messageForCorrectAnswer: Excellent! Tabs, Admonitions, and CodeBlocks are fully built-in.
questions.messageForIncorrectAnswer: Incorrect. Note that live code playgrounds require an optional first-party plugin package.
questions.explanation: Tabs, Admonitions, and standard CodeBlocks are included out-of-the-box. The live runtime playground requires installing `@docusaurus/theme-live-codeblock`.
